title.rendered: What Is a Jumbo Loan? Everything You Need to Know Before Applying

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ admin_label=”section” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ background_enable_color=”off” custom_padding=”0px||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”10px||||false|false” custom_padding=”0px||5px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Arizona’s luxury real estate market continues to flourish. From Paradise Valley’s private estates to Scottsdale’s modern hillside homes, high-value properties are in high demand. But if you’re planning to purchase a home priced above $800,000, you’ll quickly learn that conventional loans won’t always cover the full amount. That’s where jumbo loans come in — mortgage options designed specifically for high-value properties that exceed standard lending limits.

Whether you’re a first-time luxury homebuyer or a seasoned investor, understanding how jumbo loans work in Arizona can make a major difference in your approval process and long-term costs. Let’s break down what these loans are, how they work, and what it takes to qualify.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”||||false|false” custom_padding=”||4px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”What Is a Jumbo Loan?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”-4px||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

A jumbo loan is a mortgage that exceeds the conforming loan limits set annually by the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA). These limits determine how much Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac can buy or guarantee from lenders.

Any mortgage that surpasses that limit is classified as a jumbo loan. Because jumbo loans are not backed by government-sponsored entities, lenders carry the full risk — which means stricter approval standards and more comprehensive financial verification for borrowers.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_heading title=”Arizona’s 2025 Jumbo Loan Limit” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”20px||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

For 2025, the conforming loan limit in most Arizona counties is $806,500 for single-family homes. In 2026, the conforming loan limit is estimated to be over $825,000. 

That includes Maricopa County (Phoenix, Scottsdale, Mesa), Pinal County, and Coconino County.

If the amount you borrow exceeds that threshold, your mortgage falls into jumbo loan territory. In practical terms, homes in luxury neighborhoods like Paradise Valley, North Scottsdale, or Arcadia often require jumbo financing. Even fast-growing areas such as Gilbert and Chandler are seeing home values that now surpass the conforming limits.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”||||false|false” custom_padding=”5px||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”Why Jumbo Loans Have Stricter Requirements” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]The main reason jumbo loans are harder to qualify for comes down to risk.

Conforming loans can be sold to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac, freeing lenders from long-term liability. Jumbo loans, on the other hand, usually remain on the lender’s books. This means:

  • Higher risk exposure: If a borrower defaults, the lender absorbs the loss.
  • More capital requirements: Banks must hold more reserves for large loans.
  • Careful underwriting: Lenders are selective, preferring borrowers with strong credit, stable income, and low debt levels.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_heading title=”Jumbo Loan Requirements in Arizona” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

1. Credit Score
Most lenders require a minimum credit score of 700–720. Clean credit history is essential — any recent delinquencies or major derogatory marks can result in higher rates or denials.

2. Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI)
Jumbo lenders generally cap the DTI ratio at 43–45%. This ensures you can comfortably manage your mortgage payment alongside other debts.

3. Down Payment
Plan for a 10%–20% minimum down payment, though many lenders prefer 20% or higher for stronger loan terms. Something to note: IF you put between 10%-20% down, you will not have mortgage insurance. In lieu of mortgage insurance, the bank will adjust the interest rate higher. 

Some programs may allow lower down payments, but they often require additional reserves or higher rates.

4. Cash Reserves
Expect to show 6–12 months of mortgage payments in liquid reserves after closing. For a $1M loan, that could mean $60,000–$120,000 in accessible funds.

5. Documentation
Jumbo loans require full documentation:

  • Two years of tax returns and W-2s
  • Recent pay stubs
  • Bank and investment statements
  • Business financials if self-employed

6. Appraisal Requirements
High-value properties often need two independent appraisals to verify value. Lenders demand accurate market comparisons, especially in luxury neighborhoods.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_button button_url=”#getin_touch” button_text=”Get Your Jumbo Loan Quote Now” button_alignment=”center” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_button=”on” button_text_color=”#ffffff” button_bg_color=”#6CA220″ button_use_icon=”off” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_button][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto|false|false” custom_padding=”4px||3px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”Rates and Costs: Are Jumbo Loans More Expensive?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Traditionally, jumbo loans carried higher interest rates than conforming mortgages. Today, that gap has narrowed.

According to Investopedia and Bankrate, jumbo rates are often within 0.25%–0.50% of conforming loans — and sometimes even lower.

Still, the larger loan amount means even small differences can add up.
For example, a 0.25% increase on a $1M mortgage could cost around $150 more per month — over $50,000 extra across 30 years.

Additional jumbo-related costs may include:

 
  • Larger origination fees
  • Higher appraisal costs
  • Optional discount points for lower rates
  • Increased closing fees proportional to loan size

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_heading title=”Jumbo Loan Application Process” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]The steps are similar to a conventional mortgage but with deeper underwriting:

  1. Preapproval: Get preapproved early with a lender experienced in jumbo products. This helps define your buying range and signals strength to sellers.
  2. Gather Documentation: Prepare all income, assets, and tax documents early to avoid delays.
  3. Appraisal: Expect detailed evaluations, especially in custom-home markets where comparable sales are limited.
  4. Underwriting: Lenders review every financial detail, from asset sources to credit inquiries. Be prepared for additional documentation requests.
  5. Conditional Approval & Closing: After conditions are met, the loan is finalized, and you’re ready to close on your property.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”||||false|false” custom_padding=”4px||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”Risks and Considerations” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||0px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Before applying, it’s smart to understand the unique risks tied to jumbo loans:

  • Appraisal Variability: High-end homes can be harder to value accurately.
  • Market Sensitivity: Luxury homes often fluctuate more in price during market shifts.
  • Refinancing Challenges: Tighter lending standards can make future refinancing harder.
  • Liquidity Strain: The combination of large down payments and cash reserve requirements can impact flexibility.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”2px||||false|false” custom_padding=”0px||15px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”Tips to Improve Your Approval Odds” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” border_color_bottom=”#4b800a” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

  1. Check Your Credit Early: Review all three credit reports, dispute inaccuracies, and pay down revolving debt.
  2. Strengthen Your Finances: Lower your DTI and increase liquid reserves before applying.
  3. Compare Lenders: Rates and requirements vary widely among banks, credit unions, and mortgage brokers. Shop around to find the best terms.
  4. Work With Arizona Specialists: Partner with a lender who regularly handles jumbo loans in Arizona — they’ll know how to navigate appraisals and underwriting efficiently.
  5. Apply at the Right Time: Submit when your finances are at their strongest — post-bonus, after taxes, or once reserves are verified.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_heading title=”Example: Jumbo Loan in Scottsdale” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” border_color_bottom=”#4b800a” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Suppose you’re purchasing a $1.2 million home in North Scottsdale.
With a 20% down payment ($240,000), you’d finance $960,000 — a jumbo loan.

At a 7.00% interest rate, your monthly principal and interest would be about $6,384. Add taxes, insurance, and HOA, and you’re looking at roughly $7,800 per month in total housing costs.

To qualify with a 43% DTI, your gross monthly income should be around $18,300, or $220,000 per year, with $50,000–$100,000 in cash reserves after closing.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” background_color=”#f8f9fa” width=”100%” custom_margin=”||30px||false|false” custom_padding=”25px|25px|25px|25px|false|false” border_radii=”on|10px|10px|10px|10px” box_shadow_style=”preset1″ box_shadow_vertical=”1px” box_shadow_blur=”4px” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”The Bottom Line” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h3″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”24px” custom_margin=”||5px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]If you’re ready to explore jumbo financing, start by connecting with a local Arizona mortgage professional who understands the nuances of luxury home lending. The right guidance can help you secure the best rate, simplify the process, and make your dream home a reality.[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” width=”100%” custom_margin=”10px||||false|false” custom_padding=”6px||10px||false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_heading title=”FAQs About Jumbo Loans in Arizona” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_margin=”||20px||false|false” custom_padding=”||||false|false” border_width_bottom=”3px” border_color_bottom=”#4b800a” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_accordion _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” toggle_level=”h3″ toggle_font=”|600|||||||” toggle_font_size=”20px” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_accordion_item title=”1. What credit score do I need for a jumbo loan in Arizona?” open=”on” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||20px||false|false” custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|false|false” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Most lenders require at least a 700–720 credit score, but higher scores can unlock better rates and more flexible terms.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”2. Can I use a jumbo loan for a vacation home or investment property?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”||20px||false|false” custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|false|false” global_colors_info=”{}” open=”off”]

Yes. Many Arizona lenders offer jumbo financing for second homes and investment properties, though down payment and reserve requirements are typically higher.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”3. Are jumbo loan rates higher than conventional mortgage rates?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” open=”off”]

They used to be, but not always today. In competitive markets, jumbo rates can be similar or even slightly lower than conforming rates depending on your profile.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”4. How can I increase my chances of jumbo loan approval?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” open=”off”]

Focus on strengthening your credit, maintaining low debt levels, and building substantial liquid reserves before applying.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][/et_pb_accordion][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row disabled_on=”on|on|on” admin_label=”row” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ background_color=”#f9f9f9″ background_size=”initial” background_position=”top_left” background_repeat=”repeat” width=”100%” custom_margin=”||30px||false|false” custom_padding=”50px|30px|40px|30px|false|false” border_radii=”on|10px|10px|10px|10px” border_width_left=”5px” border_color_left=”#4b800a” box_shadow_style=”preset3″ disabled=”on” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.16″ custom_padding=”|||” global_colors_info=”{}” custom_padding__hover=”|||”][et_pb_heading title=”Quick Takeaways: What You’ll Learn” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” title_level=”h2″ title_font=”|600|||||||” title_font_size=”28px” custom_padding=”||2px||false|false” border_width_bottom=”3px” border_color_bottom=”#4b800a” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_heading][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

    • Multiple loan types available – fixed, ARM, conforming, and jumbo options
